description:
Several module-level docs under `crates/` span multiple sections and paragraphs after the source-comment sweep. They are reduced to one short orientation paragraph plus the contract statements no single item owns, so the workspace comment rule holds for every file.

## Background

The root `AGENTS.md` limits a module-level orientation to one short paragraph. A scan of the leading `//!` block of every Rust file under `crates/` and `dev/tools/` finds module docs of more than twelve lines; the longest are `crates/gf2-coding/src/bch/encode.rs`, `crates/gf2-core/src/gfpn/quotient.rs`, `crates/gf2-coding/src/bch/spec.rs`, `crates/gf2-kernels-simd/src/bch_encode.rs`, `crates/gf2-coding/src/bch/mod.rs` and `crates/gf2-core/src/io/field_matrix.rs`. They hold algorithm walk-throughs, selection narratives, complexity surveys that item docs own, and examples. A section stays where it states a contract that no single item of the module owns, such as a coordinate convention, a file format or a module-wide safety contract; a Rustdoc example stays where it teaches a workflow under `teaching-rustdoc-examples`.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: Each module-level doc under `crates/` and `dev/tools/` is one short orientation paragraph plus sections that each state a contract no single item of the module owns; every other section is deleted, or its content sits once on the item that owns it.
- [hard] REQ-02: Every retained or moved statement is true of the code, and public items keep purpose, panics, safety conditions and non-obvious complexity.
- [hard] REQ-03: The diff contains only comment, Rustdoc and whitespace edits and deletes more lines than it adds; Rustdoc builds without new warnings, doc tests pass and the Rust CI gate passes.
- [hard] REQ-04: A linked record lists each module doc longer than twelve lines that remains, with the contract each retained section states, produced by a committed command.
- [hard] REQ-05: The sweep completion record and its outputs are regenerated at the final commit of this change.
